servicesIntro: Bring me the messy middle: the strategy that will not land, the team pulling in three directions, or the next chapter that still feels blurry.

services.title: Find the decision inside the noise
services.summary: Move from competing opinions and endless analysis to one sharp strategic choice your team can explain — and act on.

services.title: Get the room moving as one
services.summary: Turn polite disagreement into useful tension, shared language and genuine ownership across your leadership team.

services.title: Lead the next chapter on purpose
services.summary: Step out of reactive mode with a clearer leadership stance, firmer boundaries and decisions that sound like you.

approach.title: A working session, not a performance.
approach.body: No theatre. No strategy deck that gathers dust. We name what is actually happening, find the useful edge of the problem and leave each conversation with a move worth making.

steps.label: Notice
steps.text: What is true, but not yet being said?

steps.label: Choose
steps.text: What matters enough to rule other things out?

steps.label: Move
steps.text: What is the smallest action that changes the picture?

faqs.question: How do I know whether I need consulting or coaching?
faqs.answer: You do not need to diagnose it first. Consulting is useful when the business needs a clearer choice; coaching when your leadership within that choice is the work. Most engagements use a deliberate mix of both.

faqs.question: Will this create more work for an already stretched team?
faqs.answer: The aim is subtraction. We focus on the few decisions that release energy, stop low-value work and make existing effort more coherent. I will be clear about any time commitment before we agree to proceed.

faqs.question: What if our leadership team does not agree?
faqs.answer: Agreement is not the entry ticket. A well-held process makes disagreement usable: assumptions become visible, trade-offs get named and the team can commit to a decision even when preferences differ.

faqs.question: Can we start with one conversation?
faqs.answer: Yes. A 45-minute fit call is a real working conversation, not a sales script. We will clarify the knot, decide whether I am useful and leave you with a sensible next step either way.

closing.title: Bring the knot. We'll find the thread.
closing.body: Tell me what keeps returning to the agenda. The first conversation is 45 minutes, candid and free.
